questions.prompt: A small craft meets a vessel that is not a small craft. What room must the small craft leave?
answers: Enough for the other vessel to hold course and manoeuvre
Only its own beam
None if its engine is faster
questions.explanation: The small craft must not demand that the other vessel give way.

questions.prompt: In an ordinary crossing with risk of collision, which side of your vessel is the other vessel on when you must give way under the general rule?
answers: Starboard
Port
Astern
questions.explanation: Article 6.03 bis has exceptions, including small craft in relation to other vessels and the marked-fairway boundary.

questions.prompt: Two motorized small craft meet with collision risk. What is their normal passing action?
answers: Each veers to starboard to pass port to port
Both turn to port
The faster craft always holds course
questions.explanation: The small-craft meeting provision calls for each to veer to starboard, subject to its other stated qualifications.

questions.prompt: What does an upstream vessel's Article 6.04 blue-board display indicate in a meeting?
answers: A starboard-to-starboard passing arrangement
A request to overtake
A lock priority claim
questions.explanation: It communicates the upstream vessel's indicated passing side, with the rule's conditions and exceptions.

questions.prompt: A narrow fairway cannot clearly accommodate two vessels abreast. What should you establish before entry?
answers: Whether traffic is already committed and where you can safely wait
Only the next vessel's AIS speed
How quickly you can pass in the middle
questions.explanation: Article 6.07 aims to prevent meetings where width is inadequate.

questions.prompt: When is overtaking permitted under the general Article 6.09 rule?
answers: After the overtaking vessel makes certain it can be completed without danger
Whenever the vessel astern is faster
Whenever the display shows open water
questions.explanation: The overtaking vessel must check the whole manoeuvre, not just the initial gap.

questions.prompt: What do you do when an applicable overtaking prohibition is posted for the next section?
answers: Do not start the pass in that section
Overtake if the other vessel slows
Use a sound signal to cancel the sign
questions.explanation: Article 6.11 makes the posted restriction part of the decision.

questions.prompt: May you steer through the spaces between vessels in a towed convoy?
answers: No
Yes if it is the shortest route
Only when the gap looks wider than your beam
questions.explanation: Article 6.15 prohibits entering those spaces.

questions.prompt: What is the speed rule near craft or structures vulnerable to your wash?
answers: Reduce in good time without losing safe steerage
Maintain speed to shorten exposure
Accelerate to reduce the stern wave
questions.explanation: Article 6.20 addresses damaging wash and suction.

questions.prompt: Which side of marked floating equipment at work is forbidden for passing?
answers: The side showing the prescribed red or A.1 prohibition marking
The side with a green passage marking
Either side when no traffic follows
questions.explanation: Article 6.22 bis prohibits passing on its marked closed side.

questions.prompt: When may a ferry start crossing the waterway?
answers: When other vessels' movements allow it without risk or abrupt change
Whenever it sounds a single blast
Whenever its timetable requires departure
questions.explanation: The ferry must establish a safe crossing under Article 6.23.

questions.prompt: What clearance should be kept from a vessel displaying the prescribed diving marking?
answers: A sufficient distance
Only one vessel length
None if you can see no diver
questions.explanation: Article 6.37 requires vessels to keep a sufficient distance.

questions.prompt: You are in a motorized small craft and a large convoy needs room to manoeuvre. What should you do?
answers: Leave enough room for its course and manoeuvre
Require the convoy to stop for you
Cross close ahead because you can accelerate
questions.explanation: Small craft cannot demand that other vessels give way under Article 6.02.

questions.prompt: A vessel approaches from starboard, but you are near a marked fairway boundary with that boundary to starboard. What should you check before using the simple starboard-gives-way rule?
answers: The marked-fairway course provision and any small-craft exception
Only the vessels' paint colour
Whether the other skipper waves
questions.explanation: The crossing article contains a marked-fairway boundary provision and category exceptions.

questions.prompt: An upstream vessel displays the blue board for a meeting. What must the downstream vessel understand before passing?
answers: The indicated starboard-to-starboard course and whether the rule applies
That the board grants overtaking priority
That the board replaces lookout
questions.explanation: The indicated meeting side needs to be seen and applied with Article 6.04's exceptions.

questions.prompt: The blind narrow fairway ahead is occupied by a vessel already committed. What is the safe immediate plan?
answers: Wait outside and resolve the applicable passing order
Enter to establish your place
Overtake the vessel at the entrance
questions.explanation: Avoid creating a meeting in insufficient width; apply the defined-direction and other Article 6.07 provisions.

questions.prompt: You are faster than a vessel ahead, but a narrow bridge opening is close. What is the overtaking decision based on?
answers: Whether the entire pass is safe and permitted through the restriction
Speed difference alone
Your plotted ETA
questions.explanation: The overtaking vessel must be certain it can complete the manoeuvre without danger.

questions.prompt: You intend to leave a side harbour into traffic on the main waterway. What should happen before you commit?
answers: Establish the traffic and applicable entry arrangement
Turn out immediately because you are leaving a berth
Assume the first vessel will alter speed
questions.explanation: Article 6.16 regulates entering and leaving side waterways; assess the main-waterway traffic first.

questions.prompt: Passing moored craft, your wash begins to move their lines sharply. What is the appropriate adjustment?
answers: Reduce speed in good time while retaining steerage
Increase speed to finish the passage sooner
Continue because the craft are stationary
questions.explanation: Article 6.20 requires control of damaging wash and suction.

questions.prompt: A working vessel shows a red closed side and an open side. Which route should you plan?
answers: The permitted side, with enough room and lookout
The red side if shorter
Between the workboat and its equipment
questions.explanation: Do not pass the Article 6.22 bis prohibited side.

questions.prompt: A cable ferry is about to cross. What additional hazard needs room?
answers: The ferry's crossing and its cable arrangement
Only the ferry's wake
Only the opposite bank's sign
questions.explanation: Article 6.23 includes special provisions for ferries that do not move independently.

questions.prompt: You see a marked vessel engaged in underwater diving near the fairway. What is your immediate obligation?
answers: Keep a sufficient distance and reassess your route
Pass close astern to reduce delay
Assume no diver is in the water
questions.explanation: The diving vessel marking calls for clearance under Article 6.37.

questions.prompt: What may a small craft require from a vessel that is not a small craft under Article 6.02?
answers: It may not require that vessel to give way
It may demand priority in the centre of the fairway
It may demand that vessel reverse
questions.explanation: The small craft must leave sufficient room for the other vessel to hold course and manoeuvre.

questions.prompt: In the general crossing rule, when must a vessel give way to another vessel?
answers: When it has the other vessel to starboard and collision risk exists, subject to exceptions
Whenever the other vessel is on port
Only when the other vessel is overtaking
questions.explanation: Article 6.03 bis contains the general starboard-side rule and stated exceptions.

questions.prompt: Between small craft of different categories, which craft normally gives way to a small craft under sail in a crossing?
answers: A motorized small craft
The sailing small craft in every case
Whichever craft is slower
questions.explanation: The category-specific crossing provision applies, with the marked-fairway qualification.

questions.prompt: Two small craft meet with risk of collision. What is the normal direction each veers?
answers: Starboard
Port
Neither craft should act
questions.explanation: Article 6.04 provides the small-craft meeting rule, subject to its qualifications.

questions.prompt: What course does an Article 6.04 blue board from an upstream vessel indicate to downstream traffic?
answers: A starboard-to-starboard meeting
A port turn to enter a harbour
A demand to overtake to port
questions.explanation: The upstream vessel indicates the passing course under Article 6.04.

questions.prompt: A high-speed vessel meets another vessel. What communication does Article 6.06 require for agreement on the meeting?
answers: Radiotelephony
AIS text only
A hand signal only
questions.explanation: The high-speed meeting rule calls for agreement by radiotelephony.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of Article 6.07's narrow-fairway procedure?
answers: Avoid meetings where the fairway is not clearly wide enough
Give the faster vessel automatic priority
Let every vessel enter together
questions.explanation: The article structures passage and waiting in constrained width.

questions.prompt: A waterway sign prohibits meeting in the next section. What does Article 6.08 require you to respect?
answers: The signed restriction or alternating-traffic control
Only a radio call from another vessel
Only what AIS displays
questions.explanation: Article 6.08 covers meeting prohibitions and alternate one-way traffic.

questions.prompt: Who must be certain an overtake can be completed without danger?
answers: The overtaking vessel
Only the vessel being overtaken
Only the authority controlling the bank
questions.explanation: The initial duty is on the overtaking vessel under Article 6.09.

questions.prompt: Does an empty-looking fairway cancel an applicable overtaking prohibition sign?
answers: No; the sign still governs
Yes if your vessel is faster
Yes if you sound two long blasts
questions.explanation: Article 6.11's signed prohibition remains applicable.

questions.prompt: What part of a towed convoy must you avoid entering under Article 6.15?
answers: The spaces between its vessels
Only the riverbank behind it
Only a space displaying AIS
questions.explanation: The prohibition covers the spaces within the formation.

questions.prompt: What is the core Article 6.20 obligation when your wash could damage nearby craft?
answers: Regulate speed to avoid damaging wash or suction
Maintain maximum steerage speed
Warn by radio and maintain speed
questions.explanation: Reduce in good time without dropping below a speed needed for safe steerage.

questions.prompt: A working vessel shows the prescribed red closed-side marking. May you pass on that side?
answers: No
Yes if no work crew is visible
Yes if the green side is busier
questions.explanation: Article 6.22 bis prohibits passing on the marked closed side.

questions.prompt: Before crossing, what must a ferry ensure about other vessels?
answers: They will not be forced into abrupt changes of course or speed
They can all stop instantly
They have received a timetable
questions.explanation: Article 6.23 requires a safe ferry crossing without abrupt demands on other traffic.

questions.prompt: What should you do when passing a vessel displaying the prescribed underwater-diving marking?
answers: Keep a sufficient distance
Pass close to identify the diver
Sound a general overtaking signal and proceed close
questions.explanation: Article 6.37 requires sufficient clearance.

questions.prompt: On a section with a prescribed course, what do mandatory B.1–B.4 signs control?
answers: The course vessels must follow
The colour of a private mooring
The optional shortcut
questions.explanation: The course on that section is prescribed by the displayed mandatory sign.

questions.prompt: When may a vessel turn in the waterway?
answers: When it is safe and will not force abrupt course or speed changes
As soon as it sounds a turn signal, regardless of traffic
Whenever it has crossed the centreline
questions.explanation: Article 6.13 requires a safe turn in relation to other traffic.

questions.prompt: What is the core check before leaving a berth without turning?
answers: That departure can be made safely with regard to moving traffic
Only that the engine starts
Only that the next lock is open
questions.explanation: Article 6.14 applies the turning safety framework to departure.

questions.prompt: May you pass close astern of a vessel displaying the prescribed fishing marking?
answers: No
Yes if you have sounded one blast
Yes if its gear is not visible
questions.explanation: Article 6.36 prohibits passing close behind a marked fishing vessel.

questions.prompt: A mandatory B.4 course sign governs a narrow stretch and downstream traffic is manoeuvring. You are upstream. What should you be prepared to do?
answers: Reduce speed or stop so you do not impede it
Hold speed and require traffic to move
Leave the prescribed course
questions.explanation: The upstream vessel must not impede downstream progress on a prescribed-course section.

questions.prompt: You plan to turn across the fairway, but traffic would need to brake sharply. What is the decision?
answers: Delay the turn until it can be made safely
Turn immediately after a radio call
Assume they will stop
questions.explanation: A turning vessel must not force abrupt changes from others.

questions.prompt: A marked fishing vessel is working ahead. Which proposed pass is prohibited?
answers: Passing at a short distance behind it
Keeping well clear of its stern
Waiting for a safe opening
questions.explanation: Do not pass at a short distance behind a vessel displaying the fishing marking.

questions.prompt: What may an upstream vessel need to do on a prescribed-course section approaching mandatory sign B.4?
answers: Reduce speed or stop to allow downstream traffic to manoeuvre
Ignore the prescribed course
Demand that downstream traffic reverse
questions.explanation: Upstream traffic must not impede downstream progress on that section.

questions.prompt: Before turning, what must a vessel establish about other traffic?
answers: That the turn can be safe without abrupt changes imposed on others
That it can sound a signal louder than other traffic
That the other vessels have AIS
questions.explanation: Article 6.13 sets the safety condition before a turn.

questions.prompt: Which safety framework applies when a vessel departs a berth without turning?
answers: The Article 6.13 turning framework, adapted by Article 6.14
Only the overtaking prohibition
No traffic check if the vessel is small
questions.explanation: Article 6.14 applies the turning provisions to departure, with different signals.

questions.prompt: Without the competent authority’s permission, what does Article 6.19 prohibit?
answers: Drifting
Using a marked fairway
Proceeding at safe speed
questions.explanation: Drifting requires permission under the article.

questions.prompt: Where must you avoid passing close astern of a vessel displaying the prescribed fishing marking?
answers: Directly behind that vessel
Only near a lock gate
Only on open sea
questions.explanation: Article 6.36 forbids passing at a short distance behind a marked fishing vessel.

questions.prompt: A vessel displays the Article 3.34 limited-manoeuvrability marking. What does Article 6.34 require of other vessels when meeting or crossing?
answers: Give way to it
Demand that it give way
Ignore the marking
questions.explanation: This is a special priority under the Chapter 6 rule.

questions.prompt: When are water skiing and similar activities permitted under the general Article 6.35 provision?
answers: By day and in good visibility
At night if navigation lights are fitted
In dense fog if radar is used
questions.explanation: Competent authorities may also mark sections where they are permitted or prohibited.

questions.prompt: A marked vessel with limited ability to manoeuvre crosses your course. Which Chapter 6 priority must you consider?
answers: Give way under the special-priority provision
Treat its marking as decorative
Assume it can alter promptly
questions.explanation: Article 6.34 applies to the Article 3.34 marking.

questions.prompt: What is required when meeting or crossing a vessel showing the prescribed limited-manoeuvrability marking?
answers: Other vessels give way under the special-priority rule
It must always give way to unmarked small craft
Only the vessel astern changes course
questions.explanation: Article 6.34 gives priority to a vessel showing the Article 3.34 marking.

questions.prompt: Under the general Article 6.35 rule, when may water skiing take place?
answers: By day and in good visibility
At night if the towboat has AIS
In fog if a sound signal is used
questions.explanation: Daylight and good visibility are required; local sections may also restrict it.
